header.title: China Industry 5.0 capex supercycle lifts automation, robotics, semis and industrial software suppliers

s01_bottom_line.text: Morgan Stanley expects China to spend up to $12 trillion through 2035 on infrastructure, factory upgrades and new industrial capacity under its Industry 5.0 strategy, split roughly $0.5tn infrastructure, $5.5tn factory upgrades and $6tn new capacity. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩

The article says the spending may create opportunities for companies involved in automation, robotics, semiconductors, industrial software, power systems and next-generation manufacturing technologies, across three areas: infrastructure, factory upgrades and new capacity. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩

A multi-year, multi-trillion-dollar spending cycle would raise demand volumes for suppliers of automation, robotics, semiconductors, semicap equipment and industrial software, but the article names no specific listed companies and quantifies no supplier revenue effect.

items.text: China may spend up to $12 trillion through 2035 on infrastructure, factory upgrades and new industrial capacity. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩

AI and industrial investments could boost China's potential GDP by approximately 3.5%. ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate⟩
Infrastructure spend under Industry 5.0 estimated at $0.5 trillion. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩
